stem: A straight ladder leans against a vertical wall and rests on level ground, as shown. The ladder makes a \(23^{\circ}\) angle with the wall. What is the value of \(x\)?
solution: The wall, the ground, and the ladder form a right triangle with the right angle at \(W\).
The angle \(x^{\circ}\) is an exterior angle of this triangle, so it equals the sum of the two remote interior angles: \(x = 90 + 23 = 113\).

explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the angle between the ladder and the ground inside the triangle, \(180 - 90 - 23\). Angle \(x^{\circ}\) is the angle outside the triangle, \(180 - 67 = 113\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This assumes the angle at the ground equals the angle at the wall; the two angles are not related that way.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is \(180 - 23\), which treats \(x^{\circ}\) and the \(23^{\circ}\) angle as a linear pair.

verify:
choices = {o: choices[n] for o, n in {'C': 'A', 'B': 'B', 'A': 'C', 'D': 'D'}.items()}; answer = {'A': 'C', 'B': 'B', 'C': 'A', 'D': 'D'}[answer]  # shuffled: original letters
P=figure['points']
d=lambda a,b: sqrt((P[a][0]-P[b][0])**2+(P[a][1]-P[b][1])**2)
ang=lambda a,v,b: N(acos(((P[a][0]-P[v][0])*(P[b][0]-P[v][0])+(P[a][1]-P[v][1])*(P[b][1]-P[v][1]))/(d(a,v)*d(b,v)))*180/pi)
assert abs(ang('T','W','E')-90)<0.1 and abs(ang('W','L','F')-23)<0.1
ans=90+23
assert abs(ang('L','F','E')-ans)<0.1
assert value(choices[answer])==ans==113
assert all(value(choices[k])!=ans for k in choices if k!=answer)
